note: test_shape_guard.py declares no c.block(), so no --case filter can select anything and every mutant would come back exit 3 (a sweep error, never a kill). `unfiltered` is the only honest answer for this file shape. Attribution stays strict: each declared `case` must name a function on the runner's FAILED: line. Every mutant below is CODE-DERIVED — drawn from a decision in shape-guard.py — never from reading the cases and asking what would break them.

mutants.id: M1 rule 2 reads the QUOTE-STRIPPED text (the real bug this lane already hit once)
mutants.why: `$?` lives INSIDE the double quotes, so stripping them deletes the thing being detected. This exact mistake made the scanner report 1 hit where the truth was 722.

mutants.id: M2 drop the quote strip — a search FOR the literal becomes a use of it
mutants.why: RE-AIMED after sweep 1. It first named test_grep_for_the_string_is_silent, which does NOT pin the strip: in `grep -rn "git -C"` the character before `git` is a quote, already rejected by rule 1's leading class, so the mutant survived as DEFECTIVE rather than as a coverage gap. The new case puts the mention after a SPACE inside quotes, where only the strip can keep it quiet.

mutants.id: M3 drop the heredoc strip — a payload becomes commands
mutants.why: The first scanner counted heredoc bodies as commands and manufactured hits.

mutants.id: M4 ⭐ THE LOAD-BEARING ONE — make the nag BLOCK
mutants.why: A nag that can block is not a nag. If this mutant survives, nothing in the suite prevents a future edit stranding a headless run over a style note.

mutants.id: M5 never nag at all — the silent-guard shape
mutants.why: A guard that reports nothing reads exactly like a guard with nothing to report — the SCC-77 class of failure.

mutants.id: M6 drop the tool filter — nag on every tool, not just Bash
mutants.why: Noise trains the agent to ignore the nag, which defeats the whole mechanism. RE-AIMED after sweep 1 — the fixture, not the mutant: the payload carried `file_path` only, so with the tool filter deleted the EMPTY-COMMAND guard still caught it and the mutant survived as DEFECTIVE. The fixture now carries a `command` key, which is the only shape that isolates the tool filter.

mutants.id: M7 stop failing open on unparseable stdin
mutants.original:
except Exception:
        return 0  # fails open — unparseable stdin is not a verdict about the command
mutants.why: A guard that cannot judge must allow. Raising here turns a malformed payload into a non-zero hook exit.

mutants.id: M8 NARROWING — drop run_all.py from the gate vocabulary (width, not existence)
mutants.why: An existence sweep proves a case notices behaviour is GONE; it proves nothing about the boundary, and a narrowing is the shape real regressions take. run_all.py is THE house gate — losing it from the vocabulary is the most likely real drift.
